items.title: Arab Parliament welcomes UN resolution demanding immediate halt to Houthi attacks
items.title_zh: 阿拉伯议会欢迎联合国决议，要求立即停止胡塞武装的袭击
items.summary: CAIRO — The Arab Parliament has welcomed UN Security Council Resolution 2837, which demands that the Houthi militia immediately halt its military escalation and attacks, including those targeting Saudi Arabia, civilians, commercial airports and international maritime transport. In a statement issued on Friday, the parliament said the resolution’s unanimous adoption reflects growing international recognition of the seriousness of Houthi activities and their implications for regional security, stability and freedom of international navigation. The parliament described the resolution as an important step toward unifying international opposition to the militia’s terrorist acts and continued violations. It stressed the need to translate international condemnations into decisive, practical measures to halt the attacks and hold those responsible accountable. The parliament also welcomed the extension of the sanctions regime imposed on entities linked to the Houthi militia, to prevent activities threatening the security and stability of Yemen and the wider region. It reaffirmed its support for efforts to enable Yemen’s legitimate government to exercise its constitutional responsibilities, preserve the country’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and fulfill the Yemeni people’s aspirations for security, stability, peace and development. The Arab Parliament stressed that a comprehensive political solution remains the only path to ending the Yemeni crisis.

items.title: Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain and Arab League condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.title_zh: 约旦、埃及、科威特、巴林和阿拉伯国家联盟谴责胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯的袭击
items.summary: RIYADH — Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain and the Arab League have strongly condemned the terrorist Houthi militia’s continued missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their solidarity with the Kingdom and support for measures taken to protect its security and sovereignty. In a statement issued on Thursday, Jordan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the continued attacks, most recently involving the launch of two ballistic missiles toward the Makkah region, along with missiles and drones directed at Riyadh and other areas of the Kingdom. The ministry described the attacks as flagrant violations of Saudi sovereignty, international law and the UN Charter, reaffirming Jordan’s rejection of attacks targeting civilians and civilian and economic infrastructure. Jordan also reiterated its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, stability, sovereignty, national assets, citizens and residents. Meanwhile, the Arab League strongly condemned the launch of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones toward Makkah,Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s eastern and southern regions, describing the attacks as a dangerous escalation threatening the Kingdom’s security and civilian lives. The organization stressed that targeting Saudi territory, particularly areas housing Islamic holy sites, violates the Kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, international law and the UN Charter, while infringing upon the sanctity of religious sites and provoking Muslims worldwide. The Arab League praised the effectiveness of Saudi air defenses in intercepting and thwarting the attacks and reaffirmed its support for the Kingdom’s legitimate measures to protect its territory, citizens and residents. It also warned that continued attacks would heighten regional tensions and undermine de-escalation efforts, urging the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to ensure the implementation of relevant resolutions, including 2216 (2015) and 2817 (2026). Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemned the continued attacks on Saudi territory, most recently involving ballistic missiles and drones launched toward Makkah, describing them as violations of Saudi sovereignty, international law and the UN Charter. The ministry warned that the attacks directly threaten civilians and civilian and economic facilities while undermining regional security and stability. Egypt reaffirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national assets, stressing that the Kingdom’s security is an integral part of Egyptian and Arab national security. Kuwait’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs similarly condemned the continued Houthi attacks using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones against several Saudi regions, describing them as repeated terrorist attacks that violate Saudi sovereignty, international law and international humanitarian law. The ministry rejected the attacks, warning that they threaten civilian safety and undermine regional stability. Kuwait reiterated its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to safeguard its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, emphasizing that the Kingdom’s security is inseparable from Kuwait’s security and that of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also strongly condemned the continued Houthi attacks involving ballistic missiles and drones directed toward Makkah, Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s eastern and southern regions. The ministry described the attacks as a dangerous escalation following the targeting of Madinah region days earlier, which resulted in missile fragments falling in populated areas. Bahrain stressed that the attacks violate Saudi sovereignty, international law and international humanitarian law, threaten civilian lives and infringe upon the sanctity of Islamic holy sites. The ministry praised the Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces for intercepting and thwarting the attacks, reaffirming Bahrain’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, sovereignty, citizens and residents. It also emphasized the Kingdom’s legitimate right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, stressing that Saudi security is inseparable from Bahrain’s security and the broader GCC security framework. Bahrain renewed its call for the UN Security Council to take firm action to halt repeated Houthi attacks, prevent the targeting of religious holy sites and civilian facilities, hold perpetrators and their supporters accountable, and ensure the implementation of relevant Security Council resolutions.

items.title: Saudi Arabia expresses solidarity with UAE after Fujairah crash kills 14, injures 30
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯对阿联酋富查伊拉车祸造成14人死亡、30人受伤表示慰问
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia expressed its solidarity with the United Arab Emirates following a major traffic accident in Fujairah that killed 14 people and injured 30 others, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. In a statement, the ministry extended the Kingdom’s sincere condolences and sympathy to the UAE’s leadership, government and people, as well as the families of the victims, and wished the injured a speedy recovery. The accident occurred shortly before midnight on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road at the entrance to Fujairah, when a truck collided with several vehicles, triggering a fire that spread to multiple cars, according to Fujairah Police. The Fujairah Police General Headquarters said the truck driver lost control of the vehicle, causing it to collide with another car before overturning and crashing into several vehicles that had stopped or slowed because of traffic congestion. The collision sparked a fire in the truck that subsequently spread to other vehicles, resulting in significant loss of life. Police said emergency response teams, including police, ambulance, rescue and civil defense personnel, were immediately dispatched to the scene after the operations room received a report of the accident. Emergency crews extinguished the fire, provided first aid and transported the injured to hospitals, while police secured the scene and managed traffic to ensure the safety of other road users. Authorities confirmed that 15 of the 30 injured people had been discharged from hospitals after receiving medical treatment, while the remaining 15 continued to receive medical care. Fujairah Police said the fatalities included Emirati nationals, while forensic teams were conducting DNA tests to identify several other victims. The injured included nationals of the UAE, Oman, India, Brazil, Pakistan, Jordan and Egypt. Police expressed deep sorrow over the tragedy and extended condolences to the families of those killed, while wishing the injured a swift recovery. The authorities also urged motorists to comply with traffic regulations, observe speed limits and maintain safe distances, particularly when approaching congested roads or areas experiencing slow-moving traffic. Fujairah Police said investigations and legal procedures related to the accident were continuing. The police also called on the public and social media users to avoid circulating rumors or unverified information and to rely on official sources for updates.

items.summary: WASHINGTON — The US-Saudi Business Council and the Federation of Saudi Chambers have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen ties between the business communities of Saudi Arabia and the United States of America. The agreement was signed by the Council’s Chairman and CEO Charles Hallab and the Federation’s Secretary General Sultan Al-Musallam. The signing ceremony was attended by Assistant Secretary General for International Trade at the Federation of Saudi Chambers Majid Al-Mutairi and President of the Middle East sector at Mayer Brown Company Tom Thraya in Washington, D.C. The MoU establishes a framework for enhancing communication between companies in the two countries, developing investment opportunities, and addressing challenges facing businesses in both markets. The Federation of Saudi Chambers is playing a key role in the partnership as the representative body of the Saudi private sector, ensuring that the sector’s perspectives and needs are duly considered. The memorandum sets out practical mechanisms for cooperation between the council and the federation, including facilitating trade delegation visits and communication between business leaders, supporting investments and strategic partnerships, exchanging market information and expertise, and working through relevant channels to facilitate companies’ entry into both markets and address the obstacles they encounter. A joint working group will supervise the implementation of the memorandum and develop a joint action plan. Senior representatives from both sides will meet every three months to assess progress, identify priority sectors and activities, set timelines, and assign responsibilities. Speaking on the occasion, Hallab said that the Federation of Saudi Chambers is a key partner for the council in connecting with and supporting the Saudi private sector. “This agreement allows the Council and the Federation to bring companies together, work towards common goals, and strengthen trade relations between our two countries. We value the federation’s leadership and friendship, and we look forward to further developing this partnership,” he said. The memorandum also provides for cooperation in activating the federation’s “International Business Concierge” initiative, which seeks to facilitate international business and attract and facilitate US investments in the Kingdom. Other areas of collaboration include implementing sector-specific initiatives, organizing business-to-business meetings and engagements between businesses and government entities, and supporting Saudi exports to the US market. Established in 1993 through a Saudi Royal Decree and a US Executive Order, the Saudi-US Business Council is a leading bilateral business organization committed to expanding trade and investment and promoting commercial cooperation between Saudi Arabia and the United States. The Council brings together influential business and government leaders from both countries, providing a platform to identify priorities in bilateral trade relations, unlock transformative investment opportunities, and address key challenges affecting trade and business.

items.title: Crown Prince congratulates Grenada prime minister on his re-election
items.title_zh: 王储祝贺格林纳达总理再次当选
items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman has sent a cable of congratulations to Prime Minister of Grenada Dickon Mitchel on the occasion of his re-election as prime minister.The Crown Prince expressed his sincere congratulations and best wishes for success to Mitchel, and for further progress and prosperity to the friendly people of Grenada.

items.title: Airbag defect hits 44,305 Hyundai Elantra vehicles; owners urged to get free repairs
items.title_zh: 44305辆现代伊兰特汽车出现安全气囊缺陷；车主被敦促进行免费维修
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Commerce has renewed its call for owners of Hyundai Elantra vehicles, manufactured between 2009 and 2011, to respond to recall campaigns over a defect in the driver's airbag inflator that could cause serious or fatal injuries.The ministry urged owners of the 44,305 affected vehicles remaining in Saudi Arabia to stop driving them immediately and contact authorized dealers to arrange free repairs to ensure their safety. The ministry explained that the previously announced recall covered 57,195 vehicles, of which approximately 12,890 have been repaired, representing 22 percent of the total. However, 44,305 vehicles remain unrepaired, underscoring the importance of promptly contacting authorized dealers across the Kingdom to address the defect.The ministry stressed the need for an immediate response to the recall. It urged owners to contact the authorized dealers: Wallan Company at 8001240401, Almajdouie Company at 8003040777, or Mohamed Yousuf Naghi & Brothers Group at 8001240191, to arrange the necessary repairs free of charge.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Kenya sign deal to regulate recruitment of domestic workers
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯与肯尼亚签署协议，规范家政服务人员的招聘
items.summary: RIYADH — Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development for Labor Abdullah Abuthnain received Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Labour and Social Protection Alfred Nganga Mutua at the ministry’s headquarters in Riyadh on Thursday. Several senior Saudi ministry officials and the accompanying Kenyan delegation also attended the meeting. The meeting discussed ways to strengthen cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Kenya in areas of mutual interest in the labor sector, particularly by developing cooperation mechanisms for the recruitment of domestic workers, improving the effectiveness of pre-departure training and qualification programs, and raising awareness of contractual rights and obligations. These efforts aimed to enhance the readiness of domestic workers, improve the quality of recruitment services, promote stability in contractual relations, and protect the rights of all parties. The two sides also discussed mechanisms for strengthening technical coordination, exchanging expertise and best practices in training and qualification, and improving procedures related to the recruitment of domestic workers. These measures aimed to enhance the efficiency of recruitment processes, improve their outcomes, and serve the mutual interests of both countries. Following the meeting, Abdullah Abuthnain and Alfred Nganga Mutua signed a technical annex to the agreement on the recruitment of domestic workers between Saudi Arabia and Kenya, signed on July 5, 2026. The annex is part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and develop the technical and regulatory mechanisms governing the recruitment of domestic workers. The technical annex aims to streamline procedures and reduce the costs of recruiting domestic workers from Kenya to Saudi Arabia. It also seeks to improve the efficiency of recruitment mechanisms, ensure compliance with approved regulations, protect the rights of employers and domestic workers, and regulate the contractual relationship between the two parties. The signing of the annex builds on the longstanding relations and ongoing cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Kenya, reflecting both sides’ commitment to developing their partnership in labor-related fields, improving the efficiency of the recruitment system, and promoting sustainable cooperation that serves the mutual interests of both countries.
